history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Sri Harian Vellan Sahib at Bajrour (Bajraur) village, Hoshiarpur district, marks the 1651 AD (1708 Bikrami) visit of Sri Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji, the seventh Sikh Guru, who arrived from Kiratpur Sahib with his wife and an army of 2,200 horsemen and stayed three days at the home of his devoted follower Baba Prajapati Ji. Baba Prajapati dug up the roots of wild creeping plants to feed the Guru's horse; the Guru blessed that the green vines would remain evergreen - hence 'Harian Vellan' (green vines). The date-palm tree to which the Guru tied his horse is said to still stand next to the Nishan Sahib. Finding no water nearby, the Guru struck an arrow into the ground east of the site and a spring appeared; he blessed it that bathing there with faith fulfils wishes. DiscoverSikhism also associates the shrine with a 1703 visit by Sahibzada Ajit Singh Ji - UNVERIFIED from independent sources. CSV town 'Hoshiarpur' is the district; the actual village is Bajrour, ~14 km from Hoshiarpur station on the Hoshiarpur-Garhshankar road.

name: Gurudwara Harian Vellan Patshahi VII
town_description: Bajrour (Bajraur) is a village in Hoshiarpur district, Punjab, on the Hoshiarpur-Garhshankar road in the Doaba region between the Beas and Sutlej rivers. Its gurdwara, set amid mango trees, draws devotees for its association with Guru Har Rai Ji's 1651 visit and the 'evergreen vines' legend.
